authority: Narrow inventory of agent instruction and control surfaces only. Protects the files an agent obeys; does not inventory ordinary documentation. This registry cannot create product law, choose product priority, approve work, or promote evidence.

expected_outcome.statement: Every automatic repository entrypoint routes to current tracked authority without adding an independent product doctrine.
expected_outcome.failure: Block or degrade routing when an entrypoint is missing, conflicting, or untracked.
expected_outcome.retry_exit: Repair the source or routing declaration, regenerate the catalog, and re-run validation.

expected_outcome.statement: Durable product claims resolve to one explicit source and are never inferred from methods or generated context.
expected_outcome.failure: Block a product-law claim when sources conflict or the law source is unavailable.
expected_outcome.retry_exit: Resolve the authority conflict through the product owner, then regenerate and recheck.

expected_outcome.statement: Tracked judgment methods ask evidence-bound questions and defer every material product choice to current authority.
expected_outcome.failure: Degrade the method and block it from acting as decision authority when it embeds an answer.
expected_outcome.retry_exit: Separate the method from the domain decision and re-run hostile cases.

expected_outcome.statement: Foundational policies define explicit, non-overlapping process authority and remain portable across agents and knowledge providers.
expected_outcome.failure: Fail closed on conflicting process authority, dangling references, or unsupported lifecycle state.
expected_outcome.retry_exit: Reconcile at the accountable policy owner and rerun all dependent validations.

expected_outcome.statement: Local pre-push gives bounded clean-candidate, exact-range, governed-path, and strict steering feedback; declared drift-free degradation remains explicitly local_preflight_degraded; hosted pr_merge alone authoritatively accepts repository code; scheduled monitoring detects drift without silently repairing sources.
evidence: hostile pre-push stdin and range tests
exact explained and unexplained degraded IDs
expected_outcome.failure: Block local push on missing, malformed, deletion, multi-ref, rewritten-ref, default-branch, non-fast-forward, ambiguous, dirty, ungoverned, stale, drifted, unexplained-degraded, or blocked evidence; block hosted merge separately when authoritative acceptance fails.
expected_outcome.retry_exit: Repair the candidate, range, source, or enforcement wiring and re-run local preflight plus hosted workflow validation.

expected_outcome.statement: Runtime constraints remain visible as external operating authority and never masquerade as repository product truth.
expected_outcome.failure: Stop on a same-level conflict or unavailable required capability.
expected_outcome.retry_exit: Resolve with the operator or provider; do not record runtime text as product law.

expected_outcome.statement: External skills are announced, requirement-bound, and subordinate to exact repository authority.
expected_outcome.failure: Do not use an unverified or authority-expanding skill for ChopDot decisions.
expected_outcome.retry_exit: Verify the exact capability or use a tracked repository method.

expected_outcome.statement: Each subagent has bounded ownership, preserves shared work, and returns evidence that the primary agent independently integrates.
expected_outcome.failure: Discard or bound results that exceed scope, conflict, or lack evidence.
expected_outcome.retry_exit: Clarify the task or verify locally; agent count never substitutes for proof.

expected_outcome.statement: Live branch rules, required checks, reviewer settings, bypass rights, and release environments match tracked governance intent and exact candidate evidence.
expected_outcome.failure: Report live configuration as unknown or drifted; never infer enforcement from tracked YAML alone.
expected_outcome.retry_exit: Reconcile through authorized repository settings, then independently read back the live state.
